notes: Development-only backbone-to-personalization transition audit on fresh fleets. Initial block assignment is balanced independently inside each oracle family so every family jointly covers all four blocks. The oracle-family L=7 backbone is frozen from every client's initial restricted block. Each recipient then adds nearest missing speeds until it covers 5, 8, and all 11 grid speeds; the backbone never receives these extra records. FamilyPersonalized selects ridge strength by leave-one-local-speed-out validation. LocalRegularized uses the same data and validation but an L=3 local physics prior. Metrics cover the full speed envelope at every stage. An infeasible personalized controller falls back to FamilyPool; an infeasible local controller falls back to its nearest-observed-speed L=3 physics controller, and fallback use is reported. The target result is a statistically supported crossover where personalization first beats the fixed FamilyPool; a no-crossover result is accepted.
